raw.champion: Squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx
raw.rationale: The patient's long history of smoking (27.5-pack-year) and the presence of a submucosal, ovoid nodule in the left oropharyngeal airway are highly suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma, which is a common malignancy in this region, especially in smokers.

rejected.label: Minor salivary gland tumor
rejected.why: While possible, this is less likely given the patient's smoking history and the location of the nodule.

rejected.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a type of salivary gland tumor, but the patient's presentation and history are more suggestive of a squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Lymphoma of the oropharynx
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of lymphadenopathy or other systemic symptoms that would suggest lymphoma.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease to the oropharynx
rejected.why: There is no mention of a known primary malignancy that would suggest metastatic disease to the oropharynx.
